issues.description: The method messageOnMilk is specified inconsistently across the materials. In the problem statement prose (problem_statement.md) the Part 2 text requires a signature messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and describes a return value containing the volume. However, the UML in the same problem statement (Milkable interface) declares messageOnMilk(): String (no parameters), the template usage in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java calls m.messageOnMilk() with no argument, and the solution defines the Milkable interface and implementations with a parameterless method (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java: messageOnMilk() and solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java: public String messageOnMilk()). This mismatch (parameterized vs parameterless) will confuse students which signature to implement and which form the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Recommended: update the prose in problem_statement.md to require a parameterless messageOnMilk() returning a String (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked") to match the UML, the template usage, and the solution. Alternatively, if the volume parameter is intended pedagogically, update the UML, the template calls (Main.java), the interface (Milkable.java), implementations (Seal/Goat), and all tests to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust example return values accordingly. Prefer aligning prose to the existing UML/template/solution unless adding the parameter is a deliberate teaching goal.
